'''Tamara G. Kolda''' is an American [[applied mathematician]] and former Distinguished Member of Technical Staff at [[Sandia National Laboratories]]. She is noted for her contributions in [[computational science]], [[multilinear algebra]], [[data mining]], [[graph algorithms]], [[mathematical optimization]], [[parallel computing]], and [[software engineering]].<ref name="sandianews">{{cite web|last1=Camacho-Lopez|first1=Tara|title=Sandian Named Fellow of the Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|url=http://energy.sandia.gov/sandian-named-fellow-of-the-society-for-industrial-and-applied-mathematics/|website=Sandia Energy|date=23 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905215810/http://energy.sandia.gov/sandian-named-fellow-of-the-society-for-industrial-and-applied-mathematics/|archive-date=2015-09-05|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=SC16 Invited Talk Spotlight: Dr. Tamara G. Kolda Presents "Parallel Multiway Methods for Compression of Massive Data and Other Applications"|url=http://sc16.supercomputing.org/2016/09/29/sc16-invited-talk-spotlight-dr-tamara-g-kolda-presents-parallel-multiway-methods-compression-massive-data-applications/index.html|website=SuperComputing16|accessdate=15 October 2017|date=29 September 2016}}</ref>

==Education==
Kolda received her bachelor's degree in mathematics in 1992 from the [[University of Maryland Baltimore County]] and her PhD in applied mathematics from the [[University of Maryland College Park]] in 1997.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sandia.gov/~tgkolda/cv.pdf|title=Tamara G. Kolda - CV}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Kolda was a Householder Postdoctoral Fellow at [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]] from 1997 to 1999 before joining [[Sandia National Laboratories]].

===Awards and honors===
Kolda received a [[Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers]] in 2003, best paper prizes at the 2008 IEEE International Conference on Data Mining and the 2013 SIAM International Conference on Data Mining, and has been a distinguished member of the [[Association for Computing Machinery]] since 2011.<ref name="sandianews"/><ref>{{cite web|title=Tamara G Kolda|url=http://awards.acm.org/award_winners/kolda_5055801|website=awards.acm.org|language=en}}</ref> She was elected a Fellow of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] in 2015.<ref>{{cite web|title=SIAM Fellows Class of 2015|url=http://fellows.siam.org/index.php?sort=year&value=2015|website=fellows.siam.org}}</ref> She was elected a [[Fellow]] of the [[Association for Computing Machinery]] in 2019 for "innovations in algorithms for tensor decompositions, contributions to data science, and community leadership."<ref name=facm/> She was elected to the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 2020, for "contributions to the design of scientific software, including tensor decompositions and multilinear algebra".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nae.edu/224584/National-Academy-of-Engineering-Elects-87-Members-and-18-International-Members-|title=National Academy of Engineering Elects 86 Members and 18 International Members|publisher=National Academy of Engineering|date=February 6, 2020|accessdate=2020-10-08}}</ref>
